title: Absher
body_plain: Comprehensive Report on Absher Platform 1. Executive Summary Absher platform is the comprehensive electronic gateway for the services of the Ministry of Interior and its sectors in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia. This platform aims to facilitate the completion of government transactions for citizens, residents, and visitors electronically, directly contributing to achieving the goals of Saudi Vision 2030 for digital transformation and enhancing the quality of services. The platform offers over 330 electronic and inquiry services, reducing the need to visit government offices and saving users time and effort. Absher's role extends beyond merely providing convenient services; it represents a fundamental pillar in the Kingdom's strategy towards an integrated and efficient digital government, enhancing efficiency and reducing human errors. 2. Introduction to Absher Platform 2.1. What is Absher Platform? Absher platform is the official electronic platform for providing services of the Saudi Ministry of Interior and all its various sectors. These sectors include the General Directorate of Passports, Civil Affairs, Saudi Traffic, Public Security, Police, General Directorate of Prisons, in addition to the Ministry of Municipal and Rural Affairs and Housing. The platform allows beneficiaries to complete a wide range of government transactions digitally, reflecting the Kingdom's commitment to digital government transformation. Absher is characterized by its comprehensiveness, offering over 330 electronic and inquiry services, making it a central point of contact for most daily government dealings. Absher application services are regularly updated by the National Information Center, ensuring continuous improvement and expansion of the services provided. The platform and its applications support both Arabic and English languages to meet the needs of its diverse user base. It is available via an electronic portal and smartphone applications running on "Android" and "iOS" systems. 2.2. Platform Objectives Absher is considered one of the most important contributors to achieving the objectives of Saudi Vision 2030, especially concerning digital transformation and enhancing the quality of government services provided to citizens and residents, and improving the visitor experience in the Kingdom. This transformation aims to simplify government procedures and make them more efficient and transparent. The platform aims to improve the experience of citizens, residents, and visitors by providing electronic services within an integrated system, saving time and effort, reducing bureaucratic procedures, and contributing to the elimination of paper usage. This trend towards digital decentralization contributes to building a more efficient and effective digital government, where transactions can be completed without the need to visit service centers. Furthermore, reliance on automation and providing clear data entry forms reduces the likelihood of human errors in transactions compared to traditional manual methods. This development not only enhances the operational efficiency of government agencies but also reflects a national commitment to building a strong digital infrastructure that supports comprehensive development and makes government services more accessible and reliable for all beneficiaries. 3. Absher Beneficiaries Absher platform serves a wide range of beneficiaries, divided into main categories and special target groups, to ensure digital services are accessible to everyone. 3.1. Main Categories Citizens, Residents, and Visitors: The Absher platform is designed to serve all these categories, making it a digital meeting point to meet their government needs. Absher Individuals: This part of the platform provides services tailored for citizens, residents, and visitors in their personal and family matters, such as renewing documents and managing vehicles. Absher Business: This section is dedicated to providing electronic services for individual establishments and business owners, making it easier for them to manage their workforce affairs and commercial transactions. Absher Government: This part provides services for government sector employees, enhancing the efficiency of internal operations for government entities. 3.2. Special Target Groups The platform pays special attention to certain segments of society to ensure inclusivity and accessibility of services: Mothers and Newborns: Absher provides vital services for this group, such as issuing family registers for mothers and registering newborns electronically. These services include automatic updating of family register data after newborn registration, and delivery of documents (birth certificate and updated family register) via the national address, eliminating the need to visit civil affairs offices. Pilgrims (Hujjaj): Absher offers important services for pilgrims, such as inquiring about eligibility to perform Hajj, which allows beneficiaries to confirm that they have not performed Hajj in the past five years, a prerequisite for performing Hajj. The platform also allows electronic printing of Hajj permits for the pilgrim himself, his family members, and his employees. Seniors and People with Disabilities: Absher demonstrates its commitment to inclusivity by providing smart tools and special assistance for these groups to ensure ease of platform use. For example, the personal assistant service for people with disabilities is divided into two sections: Support for the Deaf and Mute: Allows them to benefit from a sign language guide that explains the services provided by the platform and the steps to execute them. Support for the Blind: Enables them to perform some Absher platform services using Artificial Intelligence (NLP) technology via an interactive interface that allows voice commands, or selection from a menu in the application. This focus on special target groups, and the provision of advanced technological solutions such as AI to support the visually impaired, reflects a deep commitment to making digital services accessible to all segments of society, regardless of their physical abilities. This comprehensive approach not only expands the user base but also enhances the social impact of digital transformation, ensuring that no citizen is left behind in this transformation, reinforcing the government's commitment to social welfare and equal access to public services. 4. How to Register and Activate an Absher Account To benefit from the electronic services provided by the Absher platform, beneficiaries must register and activate their accounts. 4.1. Steps to Register as a New User The registration process begins by clicking on the "New User" link available at the top of the Absher platform's main page. After that, the user is asked to enter basic data, which includes the national ID number for citizens or the Iqama number for residents. It is important to note that registration requires the applicant to have an independent national ID or Iqama. If an attempt to register results in a message indicating that the ID number is already registered, the user should not register again, but rather reset their password for their existing account. 4.2. Account Activation Channels After completing the initial registration process, account activation becomes necessary for full access to Absher services. The platform offers several channels for account activation to ensure flexibility and convenience for users: Bank Account: Beneficiaries can activate their accounts through the electronic banking services of approved banks. This method provides easy activation from anywhere without the need to visit government entities. Self-Service Devices: Absher self-service devices are available at multiple locations throughout the Kingdom and can be used to complete the activation process. If fingerprint acceptance fails through these devices, the user can consult activation staff. Passport and Civil Affairs Staff: Users can visit the offices of the General Directorate of Passports or Civil Affairs to complete the activation process with the assistance of specialized staff. 4.3. Mobile Number Update After registration and account activation, the beneficiary may need to update the mobile number associated with their account. The Absher platform allows this service electronically directly through the bank's website, eliminating the need to visit branches. In some cases, if the update cannot be done through the bank, the user can visit self-service devices or activation staff to update the mobile number. It is important to note that one mobile number cannot be linked to more than one Absher account, as each account must have its own unique mobile number. 5. Integration with Other Government Platforms: Tawakkalna and NAFATH The Absher platform is distinguished by its close integration with the Kingdom's digital government services ecosystem, which enhances the user experience and provides a unified digital environment. 5.1. Absher and Tawakkalna Absher platform is an integral part of the Kingdom's digital verification system, clearly demonstrated by its integration with the Tawakkalna application. Absher provides the "Define Mobile Number for Tawakkalna Application" service. This service is specifically designed for beneficiaries (citizens, residents, visitors) who wish to register in the Tawakkalna application but do not have a verified Absher account. The steps to define a mobile number for the Tawakkalna application via Absher are as follows: Log in to the Absher platform website. Select "My Services." Select "Services." Select "General Services." Select "Define Mobile Number for Tawakkalna Application." Enter the data of the user to be defined and their mobile number. Confirm the data and submit the request. The mobile number to be defined must be linked to the user's own identity, and this service cannot be used to define the mobile number of the applicant themselves. Additionally, the beneficiary must have a digital identity on the Absher platform, and the ID number of the user to be defined must be available. Furthermore, the Tawakkalna application provides the "Tawakkalna Code" service, an electronic service for secure data sharing, where the user can generate a temporary code that grants access to their personal information without the need to share their ID number, date of birth, or mobile number. This integration reflects the government's commitment to providing seamless and secure digital services, enhancing trust in electronic transactions. 5.2. Absher and NAFATH The NAFATH platform is the unified national digital access gateway, and activating the digital identity originating from Absher via the NAFATH application enhances the security and ease of access to various government services. The steps to activate the digital identity originating from Absher via the NAFATH application are as follows: Open the NAFATH application and click on "Settings." Select "Activate Digital Identity originating from Absher." Enter the ID number and password for the Absher account. Enter the verification code sent to the mobile phone registered in Absher. Answer the verification question, which serves as an additional verification method. View the instructions for capturing biometric features to start the verification process. Automatically capture fingerprint images and complete the verification process. Wait for the fingerprint verification process to complete. Complete the activation of the digital identity originating from Absher. This integration illustrates how Absher functions as a digital identity verification hub, enabling users secure and efficient access to a wide range of government services across multiple platforms. This process enhances the cybersecurity of government services and facilitates citizens and residents in completing their transactions without the need for multiple visits or complex paper procedures. 6. Services Provided via Absher Platform (Individuals) Absher for individuals offers a wide and diverse range of electronic services covering various aspects of daily life for citizens, residents, and visitors in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia. These services exceed 330 electronic and inquiry services. These services can be categorized into several main sectors: 6.1. Passport Services Passport services are among the most prominent services offered by Absher, and they include: Issuing and Renewing Passports: Enabling citizens or their guardians to issue or renew passports for themselves or family members electronically. Issuing and Cancelling Exit/Re-entry and Final Exit Visas: This service allows for the electronic issuance and cancellation of exit/re-entry or final exit visas for family members or domestic workers. Updating Passport Information: Enabling beneficiaries to update their passport information for residents or family members. Dropping an Exited and Not Returned Worker: This service allows the employer to electronically drop a worker who has exited and not returned. Absher Travel: An optional service to enable travelers to create a travel request through the Absher (Individuals) application, and allows the vehicle owner or authorized driver to complete travel procedures via King Fahd Causeway. Tawasul Service: Enables beneficiaries to submit requests for transactions that could not be completed electronically, without the need to visit Passport Department offices. Appointment Booking: Allows individuals to book appointments at the General Directorate of Passports offices. 6.2. Traffic Services Absher covers a comprehensive range of traffic services to facilitate vehicle procedures and driving licenses: Renewing Driving Licenses: Enabling individuals to renew their driving licenses electronically with ease and speed, without the need to visit traffic offices, saving time and effort. Renewing Vehicle Registration (Istimara): Allows the beneficiary to renew vehicle registration electronically. Issuing Vehicle Repair Permit: Enables individuals to apply for a vehicle repair permit electronically. Vehicle Ownership Transfer: Allows individuals to transfer vehicle ownership between family members electronically, as well as sell vehicles and transfer their ownership. Objecting to Traffic Violations: This service enables objecting to traffic violations issued by the General Directorate of Traffic and any other authorized entity applying the traffic law and its executive regulations. Reporting Vehicle or Plate Theft: Allows individuals to electronically report stolen vehicles or lost plates. Plate Auction: Allows bidding on distinctive vehicle plates. Viewing Approved Vehicle Scrapping Centers: To identify approved centers for scrapping abandoned and damaged vehicles. 6.3. Civil Affairs Services Absher provides a range of civil affairs-related services to facilitate personal and family procedures: Renewing National ID: Allows the beneficiary to renew their national ID electronically using facial recognition technology, with the option to deliver the document to the registered national address. Issuing Family Register (for Mothers): Allows newly married Saudi women to request the issuance of a family register electronically. Newborn Registration: Enables electronic registration of newborns and requesting the issuance of a family register and birth certificate, with document delivery via the national address. Issuing Replacement for Damaged/Lost ID: Allows the beneficiary to electronically report a lost ID and issue a replacement for a lost or damaged ID. Appointment Booking: Enables the beneficiary to book a new appointment or modify a previous appointment to visit civil affairs offices. Modifying Educational Qualification: Allows the beneficiary to submit requests for modifying educational qualifications electronically. Electronic Identification Service: Enables parents to identify their children without the need to visit a civil affairs office, saving time and effort and eliminating delays in ID issuance. Linking Children's Records to Parents' Records, Correcting Marital Status, and Modifying English Name: Part of civil registry services. 6.4. General and Diverse Services In addition to the services mentioned above, Absher offers a range of general services that serve all beneficiaries: Digital Documents: Allows citizens and residents to view their digital documents through the platform. Password Reset: Enables individuals to reset their account passwords. Inquiring about General Violations: A service through which citizens and residents can view electronically registered violations by participating government entities. Absher Services Authorization: Enables registered and activated individuals on the Absher platform to issue or cancel authorization for another user (authorized person) to use specific services in Absher electronically. Inquiring about Travel Restrictions and Service Provision: This service enables individuals to inquire about existing travel restrictions and service provisions registered against them, and to view their details. Personal Assistant Service for People with Disabilities: Provides smart tools to support the deaf, mute, and visually impaired in performing their services with ease and convenience. Sector Review Authorization: Enables individuals to authorize others to review a sector and perform transactions on their behalf. Absher Reports: A service that enables citizens and residents to issue and view several reports electronically by beneficiary entities. Address Modification: To add or update the national address for use in VAT invoices by the Zakat, Tax and Customs Authority and for delivery of government documents or requests made through the Absher platform. Inquiring about Remaining Service Payment Balance: Enables individuals to inquire about their remaining service payment balance. This comprehensive list demonstrates that Absher is not just a portal for a single service, but an integrated system aimed at digitizing all essential government interactions for individuals, reflecting the Kingdom's commitment to providing smart and convenient government services. Difference Between Absher Business and Muqeem: Comparative Analysis Both Absher Business and Muqeem are vital electronic systems in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, aiming to facilitate government transactions for the private sector. While there are similarities in some of the services provided, the fundamental differences lie in the target audience and the scope of operations. 7.1. Absher Business Definition: It is an electronic platform dedicated to providing services for individual establishments and business owners. It is designed to meet the needs of the business sector, saving time and effort and reducing reliance on paper transactions or visiting official entities. Target Audience: Absher Business targets individual establishments with a total workforce of no more than 100 workers. Key Services: Absher Business enables establishment owners to perform a wide range of services related to their resident workers, including: Issuing and renewing Iqamas for residents affiliated with the establishment. Transferring services of residents affiliated with the establishment. Issuing and cancelling exit/re-entry and final exit visas. Modifying professions for sponsored individuals. Document delivery services. Authorizing others to use Absher Business to perform services on behalf of the employer. Cost: Absher Business service is not entirely free. It requires an annual subscription, and additional fees may be imposed on some specific services completed through the platform, such as Iqama issuance or renewal fees. Annual fees vary depending on the size of the establishment; for example, for medium-sized establishments (10-99 workers), fees may reach approximately 1650 Saudi Riyals, and for large establishments (more than 100 workers), fees may amount to approximately 3000 Saudi Riyals. 7.2. Muqeem Definition: It is a specialized electronic service related to the public and private sectors, offering many services related to resident affairs. Target Audience: Muqeem service targets establishments with 100 or more workers under their sponsorship, as well as all companies regardless of their workforce size. Key Services: Muqeem portal offers over 20 electronic services, and its services are largely similar to Absher Business, but it is designed to handle larger numbers of workers. These services include: Issuing and renewing Iqamas. Issuing and cancelling exit/re-entry and final exit visas. Transferring services and modifying professions. Generating reports related to the establishment and resident data. Creating authorizations. Cost: Muqeem service relies on an annual subscription system and is available in two main packages: Muqeem Operations Package: Allows for a limited number of electronic operations. Muqeem Comprehensive Package: Allows for an unlimited number of inquiry operations and electronic transactions. 7.3. Key Similarities and Differences Absher Business and Muqeem share the general goal of digitizing passport and expatriate affairs services for establishments. There is significant similarity in the basic services offered by both platforms, such as the ability to perform all services related to the General Directorate of Passports, and the ability to renew Iqamas, transfer sponsorships, and modify professions, in addition to visa services (re-entry, exit, final exit). However, the fundamental difference lies in the target audience and the size of the establishments each platform serves. Absher Business is aimed at individual establishments with a smaller workforce (less than 100 workers), while Muqeem service targets companies of all sizes and individual establishments with 100 or more workers. This precise distinction in the target audience indicates that each platform is designed to meet the needs of a specific business sector, ensuring the provision of specialized and efficient services that align with the size and nature of the establishment. Frequently Asked Questions about Absher Platform This section provides answers to some common questions that beneficiaries may have about the Absher platform, helping to clarify procedures and overcome common obstacles: How can I register for Absher? You can register for Absher through the Ministry of Interior website or through self-service devices. The process begins by clicking "New User" and entering your ID or Iqama number. How can I activate my Absher account? Accounts can be activated through several options: self-service devices, activation staff at Passports and Civil Affairs offices, or through approved banks. Can I register a mobile number to be linked to more than one Absher account? No, each account must have its own unique mobile number. I want to update my mobile number in my Absher account, what should I do? You can update your mobile number electronically directly through the bank's website, without the need to visit branches. If that is not possible, you can visit self-service devices or activation staff. What should I do if I lose my password? You can reset your password through the Absher platform. The steps include entering your ID number and registered mobile number, then answering a secret verification question. Do I need to register again to use Absher Business if I have an Absher Individuals account? No, if you have an active Absher Individuals account, you can use the same login credentials for Absher Business. Can I renew Iqama for family members while they are outside the Kingdom through the Absher platform? Yes, you can renew Iqama for family members while they are outside the Kingdom. Can a final exit visa be issued if the resident has a traffic violation? A final exit visa cannot be issued until the traffic violation is paid, according to the service terms. Can a newborn be registered electronically without the need to visit Civil Affairs branches? Yes, this can be done through the newborn registration service on the Absher platform, and the birth certificate and updated family register are delivered via the national address. How can I authorize someone to receive a national ID card through the Absher platform? You can use the service by logging into your Absher account, selecting "Authorization - Sector Review Authorization - Issue Sector Review Authorization - Civil Affairs," then filling in the authorized person's national ID number and completing the procedures. What are the requirements for renewing a national ID? It requires booking an appointment after logging into the Absher platform, and selecting "Appointments - Civil Affairs - Renew National ID Card." Are Absher Business services available on the Absher smartphone application? Yes, the "Absher Business" smartphone application is available, allowing the execution of platform services and viewing information related to employees and workforce. 9. Conclusion The Absher platform embodies a leading model for digital transformation in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, having become a comprehensive gateway for providing over 330 electronic government services to citizens, residents, and visitors. Its pivotal role in achieving the goals of Saudi Vision 2030 is evident through its continuous efforts to improve service quality, simplify procedures, and save time and effort for beneficiaries. The platform has demonstrated a deep commitment to inclusivity, by designing services specifically for groups such as mothers, newborns, pilgrims, and seniors and people with disabilities, while providing advanced support tools such as artificial intelligence and sign language. This approach ensures that digital transformation serves all segments of society without exception. Furthermore, Absher's seamless integration with other government platforms such as Tawakkalna and NAFATH enhances the effectiveness of the government's digital ecosystem and provides a unified and secure experience for users to complete their daily transactions. For the business sector, Absher offers specialized solutions through "Absher Business" for small and medium individual establishments, while the "Muqeem" service complements this system by providing similar services for large establishments and companies. This differentiation ensures that the diverse needs of the private sector are met with high efficiency. In conclusion, Absher's importance is not limited to being merely a tool for facilitating procedures; it is a vital digital infrastructure that enhances government efficiency and transparency, and supports the building of an integrated digital society in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia. Its continued development and expansion of services confirm the Kingdom's commitment to a prosperous digital future.

title: Saudi Export-Import
body_plain: Saudi Export-Import Bank (Saudi EXIM): The Financial Engine for Cross-Border Industries in 2025 The Saudi Export-Import Bank (Saudi EXIM) stands as a cornerstone of the Kingdom’s ambition to become a global logistical and industrial hub. In 2025, the bank is no longer just a financial institution; it has evolved into the "Architect of Trust" in Saudi international trade. This comprehensive guide explores how the bank operates, how foreign investors can benefit from it starting from the moment of company formation in Saudi Arabia, and the pivotal role of strategic partners like Motaded. 1. Philosophical and Operational Vision of Saudi EXIM The bank was established to bridge the financing gap in the non-oil export sector. Historically, commercial banks were hesitant to face the risks of emerging markets or international political fluctuations. This is where Saudi EXIM stepped in to provide "Risk Mitigation" solutions. Core Mandates of the Bank in 2025: Pre-shipment Financing: Providing liquidity to manufacturers to purchase raw materials and commence production. Post-shipment Financing: Converting deferred invoices into immediate cash liquidity for the exporter. Credit Guarantees: Protecting Saudi-based companies from the default of international buyers. 2. Financing Product Structure: A Roadmap for Investors The bank offers a sophisticated ecosystem of products tailored to all stages of the export process: A. Financing Products: Working Capital Finance: Designed for companies needing liquidity to execute major export orders. Buyer’s Credit: One of the bank’s most powerful tools, where Saudi EXIM provides loans to foreign entities (e.g., in Africa or Asia) on the condition that they purchase products from a Saudi-based company. Import Financing: For Saudi factories needing to import advanced machinery or technology to improve the quality of their exportable goods. B. Insurance and Guarantee Products: These products ensure that exporters can operate with peace of mind, covering risks such as: Insolvency or bankruptcy of the international buyer. Wars and political unrest in the importer's country. Currency transfer restrictions. 3. The Foreign Investor: How to Access Saudi EXIM Services? This is where the critical importance of opening a company in Saudi Arabia comes into play. To benefit from Saudi EXIM facilities, a foreign investor must navigate precise legal stages: Linking Foundation to Financing: Legal Establishment: Obtaining a MISA license and incorporating an LLC or a Joint Stock Company. Value-Added Localization: The bank usually requires products to be of "Saudi Origin" (a specific percentage of local content), incentivizing foreign investors to build full production lines within the Kingdom. Creditworthiness: The bank's evaluation depends on the company's administrative and financial efficiency. 4. The Role of "Motaded" in the Investor’s Journey with the Bank Motaded serves as a strategic partner for foreign investors seeking to leverage Saudi EXIM advantages. Its role extends beyond simple "incorporation" to "institutional readiness." Logistical and Legal Linking: Ensuring all export contracts with international parties comply with the specific insurance requirements of Saudi import. 5. title: Best Practices HR and Payroll Management in Saudi Arabia
body_plain: HR and payroll management in Saudi Arabia are two pillars of any successful organization, and in Saudi Arabia, their proper management is vital not only for operational efficiency but also to ensure legal compliance, employee satisfaction, and business growth. Powered by AI What Does HR and Payroll Management in Saudi Arabia Mean? At its core, HR and payroll management in Saudi Arabia refers to the combined activities of recruiting, onboarding, employee data administration, compensation and benefits management, legal compliance, attendance tracking, deduction processing, payroll cycle execution, taxes and social insurance calculation, and employee offboarding. While HR deals broadly with workforce strategy and employee lifecycle, payroll specifically focuses on accurate and timely payment of salaries, allowances, deductions, and statutory contributions. Both functions must work in harmony for a seamless workplace experience. In Saudi Arabia, this integration is even more critical because payroll systems must be fully compliant with national regulations such as the Wage Protection System (WPS), Saudization policies, GOSI contributions, work permits, and other labor laws that govern employee compensation and workplace rights. Overview of the Legal Framework for Payroll in Saudi Arabia Before diving into processes and best practices, it’s essential to understand the legal landscape of payroll management in Saudi Arabia. Unlike many other countries, Saudi Arabia does not impose traditional personal income tax on salaries, but has robust systems to ensure payroll accuracy, transparency, and fair treatment. 1- Wage Protection System (WPS) and Mudad One of the most important regulatory requirements for HR and payroll management in Saudi Arabia is compliance with the Wage Protection System (WPS). Through the Mudad platform, employers must submit payroll files electronically to authorities and banks to guarantee that employees are paid accurately and on time. This system reduces wage disputes and enhances transparency. 2- General Organization for Social Insurance (GOSI) Employers are required to make social insurance contributions for both Saudi and expatriate employees through GOSI. The contributions differ by nationality and cover pension, occupational hazards, and unemployment insurance. Employers must calculate these contributions correctly and submit them monthly. 3- Labor Law Compliance Saudi Labor Law defines employment contracts, working hours, leave entitlements, end-of-service benefits, and termination procedures. These provisions directly affect payroll calculations and HR policies, ensuring that employee rights are protected. 4- Saudization and Qiwa Program Saudization regulations (local employment quotas) under the Qiwa system impact HR planning and payroll budgeting, particularly for private sector employers seeking compliance with workforce nationalization goals. Failing to meet any of these requirements can lead to penalties, audits, and even suspension of government services for the company, highlighting why structured, compliant payroll management is indispensable for sustained business success. Powered by AI The HR and Payroll Process in Saudi Arabia: Step by Step Managing HR and payroll in Saudi Arabia involves careful coordination between departments and precise execution. Below is a practical overview of the typical payroll cycle, from onboarding to payment. 1- Employee Onboarding From the moment an offer is accepted, HR must collect essential documentation, including IDs (for Saudis) or Iqama details (for expatriates), bank account information, employment contract specifics, including salary and allowances, and benefit eligibility. This foundational data powers the payroll system and ensures correct processing. 2- Attendance and Time Tracking Accurate tracking of employee attendance, overtime, and leave is foundational for HR and payroll management in Saudi Arabia. This may involve biometric systems, digital time-tracking apps, or manual entries that feed into the payroll system to calculate gross wages, overtime pay, and other time-related figures. 3- Payroll Calculation Payroll calculation includes: Basic salary and allowance totals (housing, transport, etc.). Overtime and shift differentials. GOSI deductions for Saudi employees and occupational hazard contributions for all workers. Other deductions, such as loan repayments, late attendance, or statutory penalties. This calculation determines net pay for each employee. 4- Compliance and Reports Before payment distribution, HR and finance teams must run compliance checks to ensure that all calculations align with legal rules and are consistent with employee contracts. Reports linked with WPS and GOSI submissions are prepared. 5- Payment Processing Using the integrated payroll system, companies issue payments through bank transfers or payroll cards, ensuring that salaries are disbursed according to the mandated schedule (often monthly). 6- Record Keeping and Audit Trail Employers must maintain detailed records of payroll files, payslips, compliance submissions, and audit logs. These documents are essential in case of regulatory reviews or employee disputes. Read more about: Muqeem Portal Registration: Step-by-Step Guide for Expats HR and Payroll Technology: Systems That Make a Difference One of the most impactful transformations in HR and payroll management in Saudi Arabia is the adoption of advanced digital systems that replace manual processes. Integrated HRMS and Payroll Solutions Modern HRMS platforms offer complete solutions that combine employee data management, attendance tracking, payroll automation, leave requests, and compliance reporting into one centralized system. This integration simplifies data flow, reduces errors, and saves labor hours. Cloud-Based Payroll Platforms Cloud payroll systems allow HR and finance teams to access data securely from anywhere, enable real-time updates, and support scalability as the company grows. They also offer enhanced security features like encryption and role-based access. Specialized Payroll Software Countries like Saudi Arabia, with specific compliance needs, benefit from payroll software tailored to local labor laws and regulatory platforms such as WPS and GOSI. These solutions automatically incorporate rule updates and help ensure compliance. Benefits of HR and Payroll Software Automated payroll calculations with minimal human input. Reduced errors in pay and compliance reporting. Integrated leave and attendance management. Seamless data integration between HR, finance, and compliance units. Improved transparency for employees and management. Ultimately, investing in the right technology enhances operational accuracy and improves the employee experience. Powered by AI Best Practices for HR and Payroll Management in Saudi Arabia Now that we understand the fundamentals, here are some practical best practices that HR professionals should adopt to excel in managing HR and payroll in Saudi Arabia. 1- Stay Up to Date on Regulatory Changes Laws and compliance requirements often evolve. Regularly monitoring announcements from the Ministry of Human Resources and Social Development (MHRSD), GOSI, and related authorities helps prevent compliance gaps. 2- Conduct Regular Audits Internal audits of payroll calculations, attendance records, and system configurations can catch errors before they affect payroll runs or trigger compliance issues. 3- Document Policies Clearly Ensure that compensation policies, overtime rules, benefits, termination payments, and end-of-service procedures are documented, routinely reviewed, and communicated to employees. 4- Promote Transparency Clear communication with employees about salary structure, pay dates, deductions, and benefits builds trust and reduces queries or conflicts related to payroll. 5- Train HR and Finance Teams Regular training for teams involved in payroll processing ensures familiarity with systems, compliance standards, and reporting obligations. Learn more about: VAT Registration in Saudi Arabia: Businesses and Compliance Common Challenges in HR and Payroll Management and How to Overcome Them While effective HR and payroll management are rewarding, organizations often face challenges: 1- Manual Errors and Inaccurate Calculations Manual payroll processing increases the risk of errors, especially with complex allowances and deductions. Automation through payroll software significantly reduces this risk. 2- Compliance Complexity Navigating multiple government systems like WPS, GOSI, and Saudization quotas can be challenging. Establishing clear processes and leveraging technology that automatically aligns with these systems helps organizations stay compliant. 3- Data Security and Privacy Payroll data includes sensitive personal information. Robust security measures, encrypted storage, and restricted access protocols protect employee data from breaches. What distinguishes Motaded? Motaded stands out as a comprehensive business and HR partner in Saudi Arabia by offering end-to-end services that simplify complex administrative, regulatory, and human capital challenges for both local and foreign companies. We provide tailored HR services, including recruitment, payroll management, government relations, visa and residency processing, and compliance support through platforms such as Muqeem, Qiwa, and GOSI, enabling businesses to focus on growth rather than paperwork. What truly distinguishes Motaded is its ability to integrate government relations (GRO/PRO), employee lifecycle support, and strategic workforce solutions under one roof, coupled with flexible packages that scale with client needs, making it a one-stop solution for HR and operational compliance in the Saudi market. Powered by AI FAQs About HR and Payroll Management in Saudi Arabia What is the ideal payroll cycle for Saudi companies? There is no one-size-fits-all; typically, monthly payroll is aligned with contract terms and WPS requirements, but considerations vary by industry and contract type. How should companies handle wage disputes or payroll grievances? Best practice is a documented payroll dispute resolution policy that outlines steps for employee reporting, investigation, and correction. Can expatriate salaries be paid in currencies other than the Saudi Riyal? Payroll in Saudi Arabia is legally required in SAR unless special arrangements are approved for remote workers or expatriates under specific payroll frameworks. What happens if GOSI payments are late? Late or incorrect social insurance contributions may result in penalties and the loss of license privileges, requiring corrective submissions and potentially fines. Are bonuses and incentives subject to WPS? Bonus structures must be carefully aligned with contractual terms and WPS reporting rules to ensure they are included correctly in payroll files. Conclusion In summary, we have established ourselves as a trusted partner for companies navigating HR and payroll management in Saudi Arabia, offering comprehensive solutions that support compliance, streamline operations, and free your team to focus on growth and strategic priorities. Contact Motaded today for a tailored consultation and discover how our expert team can help your business thrive in Saudi Arabia’s competitive market. Whether you need full HR outsourcing, payroll accuracy, or visa assistance, we’re here to make your HR journey smooth and successful.

title: Future Trends in Corporate Responsibility Practices
body_plain: Future Trends in Corporate Responsibility Practices Corporate responsibility (CR) is evolving rapidly as businesses worldwide respond to increasing demands for ethical practices and sustainable strategies. In today's interconnected world, businesses are under more scrutiny than ever before, facing pressure not only from consumers but also from investors, governments, and the public. This article delves into the upcoming trends in corporate responsibility, providing insights into how companies can adapt to these changes to maintain a competitive edge while fulfilling their social obligations. As businesses navigate these waters, understanding and implementing effective CR strategies can differentiate them in the marketplace. This overview highlights Future Trends in Corporate Responsibility Practices across regions and summarizes corporate responsibility trends that leaders should watch. Corporate responsibility refers to a company's commitment to conduct its business ethically and sustainably. This encompasses a wide range of activities, including environmental stewardship, social equity, and economic viability. The goal is to operate in a manner that enhances society and the environment, rather than contributing to their detriment. More than just a set of guidelines, CR represents a mindset that influences every aspect of a company's operations, guiding decisions and shaping corporate culture. A robust CR framework can help businesses mitigate risks, attract talent, and enhance their brand reputation. Staying alert to social responsibility trends ensures these efforts remain relevant and effective. CR Meaning in Business In the business context, CR means integrating social and environmental concerns in the company's operations and interactions with stakeholders. It's about more than just philanthropy; it's about embedding these values into the core of business strategy and operations. Companies that prioritize CR often see it as a vehicle for innovation, allowing them to uncover new business opportunities and create value in unexpected ways. By aligning business objectives with broader societal goals, companies can drive long-term sustainability and profitability, ensuring that their operations contribute positively to society at large. In short, this is the cr meaning in business, linking values to strategy and execution. Emerging Trends in Corporate Responsibility The landscape of corporate responsibility is shifting, influenced by globalization, technological advancements, and changing consumer expectations. These social responsibility trends reflect a broader movement toward measurable impact and transparent reporting. Here are some of the key trends that companies should be aware of: 1. Increased Transparency and Accountability As consumers become more informed, they demand greater transparency from companies. Businesses are now expected to be open about their practices and impacts. This includes disclosing environmental footprints, sourcing methods, and labor practices. Companies that embrace transparency and hold themselves accountable are more likely to gain consumer trust and loyalty. Moreover, transparency fosters a culture of openness and honesty, encouraging businesses to continuously improve and innovate. By adopting robust reporting and disclosure practices, companies can not only meet regulatory requirements but also build stronger relationships with stakeholders. 2. Focus on Sustainable Business Strategies Sustainability is no longer just a buzzword; it's a critical component of corporate responsibility. Companies are increasingly adopting sustainable business strategies to minimize environmental impact and ensure long-term viability. This includes reducing carbon emissions, implementing energy-efficient practices, and embracing circular economy principles. Sustainable strategies often lead to cost savings, improved operational efficiency, and enhanced brand loyalty. Furthermore, as global awareness of environmental issues grows, businesses that demonstrate a commitment to sustainability are better positioned to attract eco-conscious consumers and investors who prioritize environmental, social, and governance (ESG) criteria. 3. Integration of Ethical Corporate Practices Ethical corporate practices are gaining traction as businesses recognize the importance of operating with integrity. This involves adhering to ethical guidelines in all areas of operation, from supply chain management to marketing practices. Companies are also focusing on ethical treatment of employees, promoting diversity and inclusion, and ensuring fair wages and working conditions. By fostering a culture of ethics, businesses can enhance employee morale and productivity while reducing the risk of legal issues. Ethical practices also resonate with consumers, who are increasingly choosing to support companies that align with their personal values and demonstrate a commitment to social justice and equality. The Role of Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) Corporate social responsibility (CSR) is a key aspect of corporate responsibility that focuses on the company's role in society. It involves initiatives that contribute to social welfare, such as community development projects, charitable contributions, and volunteer programs. CSR initiatives are not just about giving back; they are strategic efforts that align with a company's mission and values, designed to create positive social change while enhancing the company's reputation. CSR Best Practices The following CSR best practices can guide practical action: Community Engagement: Building strong relationships with local communities through engagement and collaboration. This can involve partnering with local organizations, supporting local causes, and actively participating in community events to create a sense of shared value. Environmental Initiatives: Implementing programs to reduce environmental impact, such as waste reduction and resource conservation. Companies can adopt green technologies, promote recycling, and engage in reforestation projects to demonstrate their commitment to environmental stewardship. Employee Well-being: Prioritizing employee health and happiness through supportive workplace policies and benefits. By fostering a supportive and inclusive work environment, companies can boost employee satisfaction and retention, creating a motivated and productive workforce. The Evolution of Business Ethics Business ethics have evolved significantly over the years. Today, there's a greater emphasis on ethical conduct and corporate governance. This business ethics evolution is driven by a combination of regulatory requirements and consumer expectations. As a result, businesses are increasingly expected to operate with transparency, fairness, and accountability, ensuring that their actions align with societal values and norms. Key Areas of Focus Anti-corruption Measures: Implementing policies to prevent bribery and corruption in business dealings. Companies are investing in compliance programs and training to ensure that employees understand and adhere to ethical standards. Fair Trade Practices: Ensuring fair treatment of suppliers and partners, often through fair trade certifications. By supporting ethical sourcing and production methods, companies can contribute to equitable economic development and foster long-term partnerships. Data Privacy and Security: Protecting customer data and maintaining privacy in all business operations. With the rise of digital technologies, safeguarding personal information has become a critical aspect of maintaining consumer trust and complying with legal obligations. The Importance of CR Numbers and Certificates In many countries, including Saudi Arabia, companies are required to obtain a Commercial Registration (CR) certificate, also known as a commercial registration certificate. This certificate serves as an official recognition of the company's legal status and compliance with local regulations. It is a crucial component of corporate identity, providing businesses with the legal framework necessary to operate and engage in commercial activities. In some guidance, you may see this referred to as the commercial registration certificate saudi arabia. CR Number Saudi Arabia The CR number is a unique identifier for businesses operating in Saudi Arabia. It is crucial for legal recognition and is often required for various business transactions and regulatory compliance. Often searched as "cr number saudi arabia," the identifier is tied to the company’s registration records and licensing. Obtaining a CR number can enhance a company's credibility and facilitate access to local markets and resources. Banks, marketplaces, and vendors may ask for a CR copy for onboarding and verification, and the CR of the company commonly appears on invoices and contracts. Additionally, compliance with CR requirements ensures that businesses operate within the legal framework, reducing the risk of penalties and enhancing corporate reputation. This process is closely linked to the commercial registration certificate and, in local documentation, the commercial registration certificate Saudi Arabia. Future Directions in Corporate Responsibility The future of corporate responsibility is likely to be shaped by several factors, including technological advancements, regulatory changes, and evolving consumer expectations. Here are some potential directions: 1. Digital Transformation Technology will play a critical role in the future of corporate responsibility. Digital tools can enhance transparency, improve supply chain management, and enable better tracking of environmental impacts. From blockchain technology to artificial intelligence, digital innovations can streamline CR efforts, making them more efficient and effective. By leveraging technology, companies can gain valuable insights into their operations, allowing for more informed decision-making and targeted sustainability initiatives. 2. Increased Regulation Governments around the world are implementing stricter regulations regarding corporate responsibility. Companies will need to stay informed and adapt to these changes to remain compliant and competitive. Regulatory frameworks are evolving to address pressing global challenges, such as climate change and human rights, requiring businesses to adopt more rigorous standards and practices. By proactively engaging with regulators and participating in policy development, companies can help shape the regulatory landscape and ensure their interests are represented. 3. Consumer-Driven Change Consumers are becoming more conscious of the impact of their purchases. Companies will need to align their practices with consumer values to succeed in the marketplace. This shift towards ethical consumption is driving companies to innovate and adopt sustainable practices that resonate with their target audience. By actively engaging with consumers and understanding their preferences, businesses can tailor their offerings to meet demand for responsible products and services, ultimately enhancing brand loyalty and market share. Conclusion Corporate responsibility is no longer optional; it is a fundamental aspect of business success. By understanding and embracing the latest trends in corporate responsibility, companies can not only meet regulatory requirements but also build a strong reputation and foster long-term success. As businesses continue to evolve, those that prioritize ethical practices, sustainability, and social responsibility will lead the way in shaping a more equitable and sustainable future. Companies that integrate CR into their core strategies are better positioned to navigate the complexities of the modern business environment, driving positive outcomes for their stakeholders and society as a whole.

title: Ministry of Investment (MISA): Vision, Sectors, Services
body_plain: The Ministry of Investment (MISA) represents one of the most strategic institutions in Saudi Arabia’s economic transformation agenda. Established to fuel investment, attract global capital, and drive the diversification of the economy under Vision 2030, MISA plays a central role in shaping the future of business in the Kingdom. Powered BY AI What Is the Ministry of Investment (MISA)? The Ministry of Investment (MISA), formerly the Saudi Arabian General Investment Authority (SAGIA), was elevated to full ministerial status in 2020 by royal decree as part of Saudi Arabia’s strategic effort to unify and elevate investment governance. At its core, MISA is the government body responsible for regulating, promoting, and facilitating both domestic and foreign investment in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia. It serves as a central authority with jurisdiction over investment policy, licensing, investor support, and economic competitiveness, making the Kingdom a welcoming destination for global capital. His Excellency Khalid Al-Falih, as Minister of Investment, leads MISA with the mandate to attract strategic investment, support private sector growth, and expand opportunities across a diverse range of economic sectors. learn more about: Ministry of Investment in Saudi Arabia MISA Historical Evolution and Strategic Importance MISA traces its roots back to the General Investment Authority, created in 2000 to improve access for foreign investors. Over time, the Saudi government recognized the need for a more powerful and cohesive investment institution, and in 2020, the agency was transformed into the Ministry of Investment (MISA). This change elevated its capabilities, expanded its mandate to include both domestic and foreign capital, and integrated it directly into Saudi Arabia’s economic policy framework. This transformation positioned MISA at the heart of Saudi Vision 2030, a bold reform initiative aimed at reducing dependence on oil, diversifying the economy, and creating sustainable long-term prosperity. As such, MISA plays a central part in delivering the Kingdom’s National Investment Strategy, which seeks to increase investment quality and scale, expand foreign direct investment (FDI), and unlock opportunities across priority sectors. Mission and Core Objectives The Ministry of Investment (MISA) operates with several clearly defined goals: Promote and Attract Investment MISA actively markets Saudi Arabia as a global investment destination and encourages both domestic and foreign companies to establish and expand their operations in the Kingdom. Develop a Competitive Investment Environment By setting policies, reviewing regulatory frameworks, and removing procedural barriers, MISA enhances the Kingdom’s competitiveness and investor appeal. Issue Investment Licenses MISA is responsible for issuing the necessary investment licenses that allow foreign entities to legally operate in Saudi Arabia, a critical step in business setup. Support Investors Directly The ministry offers a range of services, including sector insights, regulatory navigation support, business incorporation guidance, and aftercare services for investors. title: Saudi Ministry of HR Increases Saudization in Engineering and Procurement for 2026: A Compliance Guide by Motaded Ltd
body_plain: Saudi Ministry of HR Increases Saudization in Engineering and Procurement for 2026: A Compliance Guide by Motaded Ltd In pursuit of the ambitious goals of Saudi Vision 2030 to empower national talent, the Ministry of Human Resources and Social Development (HRSD) has issued landmark decrees to increase Saudization (localization) in two vital sectors: Engineering Professions and Procurement Professions. As a strategic partner for investors in the Kingdom, Motaded Ltd provides this comprehensive news analysis and procedural guide to ensure your business remains compliant with these new regulatory updates. I. Raising Engineering Saudization to 30% and Increasing the Minimum Wage The engineering sector is the backbone of the Kingdom’s construction and industrial renaissance. To ensure the active participation of Saudi engineers, the first decree introduced decisive measures affecting the core operational workflows of enterprises. 1. Details of the Engineering Decree and Timeline Target Saudization Rate: The rate has been raised to 30% of the total engineering workforce within a firm. Minimum Wage: To be counted toward the Saudization percentage, a Saudi engineer’s salary registered in GOSI must not be less than SAR 8,000. Implementation Date: The decree officially takes effect on December 31, 2025, making 2026 the year of full compliance. Target Entities: This applies to all private and non-profit organizations employing five or more engineers in the targeted roles. 2. Targeted Engineering Professions (46 Specialized Roles) The decree covers a wide spectrum of disciplines that intersect with infrastructure, mining (where Motaded Ltd operates alongside Slow Shan Ltd), and manufacturing. Key roles include: Architectural and Civil Engineering: Architect, Civil Engineer, Urban Planner. Power and Mechanical Engineering: Power Generation Engineer, Mechanical Engineer, HVAC Engineer. Electronic and Technical Engineering: Electronics Engineer, Telecommunications Engineer, Computer Engineer. Specialized Engineering: Marine Engineer, Vehicle Engineer, Sanitary Engineer, and Chemical Engineer. Important Note: The decree mandates that all engineers (Saudi and expatriate) must obtain Professional Accreditation from the Saudi Council of Engineers (SCE). II. 70% Saudization in Procurement: A Revolution in Supply Chains The second decree aims to redefine the procurement and logistics sector, a field that global and local giants rely on to manage their financial and commodity flows. 1. Objectives and Target Ratios Saudization Rate: Increased to 70%, reflecting the abundance of qualified national talent in this field. Effective Date: The decree enters into force on November 30, 2025. Target Entities: Firms employing three or more workers in the specified procurement professions. 2. Targeted Professions in Procurement and Logistics Twelve core professions have been identified within the Unified Saudi Classification of Occupations: Purchasing Manager (Procurement Manager). Purchasing Representative (Procurement Delegate). Contracts Manager. Tenders Specialist. Procurement Specialist. Logistics Services Manager. Warehouse Manager and Storekeeper. E-commerce Specialist. Market Research Specialist. Private Brand Supply Specialist. III. Motaded Ltd’s Strategic Analysis: Impact on the Business Sector As specialists in commercial business setup in KSA, we at Motaded Ltd believe these decisions are not just numbers; they reflect the maturity of the Saudi labor market. Value Added by Investing in National Talent Operational Sustainability: Reducing reliance on external recruitment minimizes the risks associated with global human supply chain fluctuations. Leveraging "HADAF": Compliant firms will receive priority access to localization support programs provided by the Human Resources Development Fund (HRDF). Improved Work Quality: National talent in leadership roles, such as "Procurement Manager," enhances understanding of the local market and improves negotiation leverage with local suppliers. Challenges and Mitigation Strategies for Investors Motaded Ltd recognizes that raising the minimum wage to SAR 8,000 for engineers may pose a sudden financial burden. We recommend the following: Benefits Restructuring: Integrating allowances into the basic salary to ensure the regulatory minimum is met. Early Planning: Immediately starting to attract and train new graduates during the 6-month grace period. IV. Motaded Ltd’s Procedural Guide for 2026 Compliance To avoid regulatory penalties, enterprises must follow these steps precisely: 1. Review GOSI Data Ensure that job titles for all employees perfectly match their actual duties and the Unified Classification of Occupations. Any discrepancy may lead to the employee being excluded from the Saudization count or result in "Fake Saudization" violations. 2. Mandatory Professional Accreditation Every expatriate engineer in your firm must hold a membership with the Saudi Council of Engineers. Without this accreditation, the firm cannot renew work permits or transfer services. Furthermore, Saudi engineers will not be counted in the percentage unless they are accredited. 3. Integration with "Meza" (MISA) For foreign investors who have obtained a Saudi Arabia investment license, compliance with Saudization rates is a prerequisite for maintaining the privileges of the "Meza" platform. V. The Role of the Motaded Digital Platform in Compliance Management As part of our 2026 vision, the Motaded Digital Platform will play a pivotal role in simplifying these procedures. The platform will provide smart tools for investors, including: Smart Dashboard: To monitor Saudization rates in real-time (Hiring Dashboard). Early Warning System: Alerts you when the firm approaches the "Red Zone" or when professional accreditations need renewal. Integration with ZATCA and GOSI: Ensuring that payroll and tax reports accurately reflect true Saudization rates. VI. Government Support Packages and Incentives The Ministry of Human Resources has emphasized that compliant firms will not be left alone; they will benefit from: Wage Subsidies: Programs covering 30-50% of Saudi employees' salaries for a specific period. On-the-Job Training: State contributions to the training costs of new engineers. Procurement Priority: Earning extra points in the government procurement system for firms with high Saudization rates. VII. Conclusion: The Future of Business Starts with Compliance The new decrees for engineering and procurement Saudization are a call for all enterprises to elevate their professional standards. At Motaded Ltd, we believe the successful investor turns regulatory challenges into growth opportunities. If you are looking for specialized consultancy on how to restructure your workforce to align with these decrees, or if you are in the Saudi company incorporation phase and wish to build a compliant team from day one, our team at Motaded Ltd is ready to serve you. Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ) - Saudization 2026 Q: Does the SAR 8,000 minimum apply to existing engineers? A: Yes. To be counted in the 30% ratio, their registered salary must be adjusted to the new minimum before the implementation date. Q: What if I have only two engineers in my firm? A: The engineering decree does not apply to you yet, as it targets firms with five or more engineers. Q: How can I get the full procedural guide? A: You can visit the HRSD website or contact our advisors at Motaded Ltd for an annotated copy.

body_plain: Launch of the Final Phase: Mandatory Electronic Transfer of Domestic Workers' Salaries in Saudi Arabia for 2026 The Ministry of Human Resources and Social Development (HRSD) has officially announced the commencement of the fifth and final phase of the decree mandating the electronic transfer of domestic workers' salaries, effective January 1, 2026. This date marks a significant milestone, as the mandate now applies to all employers across the Kingdom without exception, regardless of the number of workers they employ. The Digital Transformation Journey: From Gradual Phases to Full Mandate The decision for the electronic transfer of domestic workers' salaries 2026 was not accidental; it is the result of a deliberate strategy implemented by the Ministry throughout 2025 to ensure the readiness of the community and banking systems: Phase Two (January 2025): Targeted employers with four or more workers. Phase Three (July 2025): Included employers with three or more workers. Phase Four (October 2025): Applied to those with two or more workers. Phase Five (January 1, 2026): Full mandate for all employers, even those with a single domestic worker. II. Objectives of the Decree and Impact on Contractual Transparency The decree aims to regulate the contractual relationship and safeguard the rights of both parties. The Ministry of Human Resources emphasizes that this step contributes to: Documentation of Wage Payments: Eliminating labor disputes related to delayed or unpaid salaries. Enhancing Transparency: Creating a verified digital record for every financial transfer made through official channels. Compliance with International Standards: Raising the Kingdom’s ranking in labor rights and financial transparency indices. The Role of the "Musaned" Platform The Musaned platform is the primary driver of this transformation. It links the employer with the worker and provides the necessary tools to complete transfers via banks and approved digital wallets (such as STC Pay, Urpay, and others). III. Linking Core Data The process begins by linking the domestic worker’s mobile number to their Residency ID (Iqama) via the "Absher" platform. This is essential for receiving financial notifications and digital identity verification. 2. Most Saudi banks now offer a "Domestic Worker Account" option, which is easy to open and does not require a minimum balance. 3. Using the "Salary Transfer" Feature in Banking Apps On payday, the employer uses the specific "Domestic Worker Salary Transfer" option within their banking app. This is distinct from a regular transfer, as it is immediately recorded in the Ministry's systems as a "Verified Wage Payment." IV. Benefits of Electronic Transfer for Employers and Workers The electronic transfer of domestic workers' salaries 2026 provides tangible benefits beyond mere legal compliance: Benefits for the Employer: Legal Protection: Digital records are the only definitive evidence accepted by labor courts in case of claims of non-payment. Streamlined Procedures: Facilitates the issuance of Exit-Reentry or Final Exit visas, as systems automatically verify that all salaries have been paid. Electronic Authorization: The ability to authorize family members to execute transfers ensures payment continuity even if the employer is traveling. Benefits for the Worker: Financial Security: Guarantees that the salary is received on time and in full. Easy International Remittance: Enables workers to send money to their families in their home countries with a single click at competitive exchange rates via digital wallets. Financial Inclusion: Integrates workers into the banking system, making it easier for them to manage their savings. V. With our upcoming launch of the Motaded Digital Platform in mid-2026, we aim to provide integrated solutions that intersect with these government initiatives. Legal Awareness: We strive to educate our clients about the latest updates from the Musaned platform and the Ministry of Human Resources to ensure a dispute-free work environment. VI. Regulatory Penalties for Non-Compliance The Ministry of Human Resources confirms that failure to comply with the electronic salary transfer decree may expose the employer to several consequences, including: Financial Fines: Imposed for every month of delay or for every worker whose salary was not transferred electronically. Suspension of Services: Employers may be barred from issuing new visas or transferring worker services.
